data.rationale: The commit addresses an issue where LATERAL subqueries containing lateral references hidden inside join alias Vars (such as whole-row references to a join) were incorrectly pulled up by the optimizer. This happened because pull_up_simple_subquery() re-checked pull-up safety before flattening these alias Vars, causing lateral dependencies to be missed. The fix ensures that flattening occurs before the safety re-check for both the target list and the jointree quals of lateral subqueries. The grammar is extended to allow aliasing join constructs and referencing these aliases as whole-row variables in expressions like IS NULL or text casts, which triggers the logic for join alias Var flattening.
data.grammar_fragment: from_item : <1> joined AS @derived_alias ; expr<bool> : <0.2> "(" @derived_alias IS NOT?0.5 NULL ")" ; expr<text> : <0.2> "(" @derived_alias "::text" ")" ;
seeds: SELECT t0.c0, ss.res FROM t0, LATERAL (SELECT (j IS NULL) as res FROM (t1 LEFT JOIN t2 ON t1.c0 = t2.c0) j) ss; SELECT t0.c1, ss.val FROM t0, LATERAL (SELECT 1 AS val FROM (t1 LEFT JOIN t2 ON t1.c0 = t0.c0) j WHERE j IS NOT NULL) ss;
SELECT t1.c0, sub.txt FROM t1 LEFT JOIN LATERAL (SELECT j::text AS txt FROM (t0 LEFT JOIN t3 ON t0.c0 = t3.c0) j WHERE length(j::text) > 5) sub ON true;
